note: Reads project the parsed model into one camelCase shape: paragraphs carry id, style, alignment, text and per-run text, bold, italic, underline, strike, fontSize in points, fontFamily (ascii, else hAnsi), color and styleId, with absent values as null; tables, sections, headers and footers nest those paragraphs. runHighlights records each paragraph's id with the highlight of each of its runs, and cellMerges each table's rows of cells with gridSpan and vMerge; both run on TS and Rust only, since the Python binding exposes neither. Body paragraphs include table cells and block content controls in document order. Exports and content-control reads take the camelCase options of every target unchanged. Edits replace one whole paragraph's text through a session with client id 1; the receipt records story, start, end and revisionIds, since paragraph keys are session-local. Every save sets updateModifiedDate false, so docProps/core.xml keeps its source bytes; Rust and Python pass the clock in now, while TypeScript's save reads wall time, which with modified-date updates off does not reach the saved file. readEdited reads the text of the paragraph with paraId from the edited document and the text of the body story from the parsed model (on TypeScript after a save with the parity options and a re-parse; the engine reads its model), whose paragraphs leave out table cells and keep block content controls, joined by newlines without empty paragraphs. readEdited leaves out the paragraphs its exceptParaIds name, 00000019 and 00000016, because TypeScript's save of an edited document moves the page break inside a run of 00000019 to the start of 00000016, and pageBreakMove, on TS only, pins both paragraphs' texts after that save (a page break as \f); a fix of the move removes the exception and the pin in the same change. Any other read after an edit follows openSaved, which reopens the bytes the last save wrote. renderPng records width, height and the count of pictures drawn as placeholders, never pixels. replaceParagraphTextAt addresses a body paragraph before the first table, where every target counts paragraphs alike. save records each part of the saved package by name, sha256 and byteLength of its uncompressed bytes; saveReport records keptUnchanged and structureDropped with the same parts record of the save the report belongs to. engineSteps continue the run on Rust and Python only and compare with engine-expected.json. Both goldens record the sha256 of this file's bytes.
